basis: PURA-related encephalopathy defines the disease; persistent ptosis represents eyelid dysfunction in 30-79%. Respiratory distress alone does not establish pulmonary injury.

decisions.ocular: involved: ptosis is persistent eyelid dysfunction, reported in 30-79%; eyelids fall within the ocular axis.

basis: Autoimmunity with arthritis and cutaneous lesions as major diagnostic criteria; nephritis affects ~30-60%. Hematologic and oral involvement omitted by the four-axis cap.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: inflammatory cutaneous lupus lesions are major diagnostic criteria; malar rash occurs in 44/57 patients.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: inflammatory arthritis is a major diagnostic criterion and occurs in 30-79% in the supplied HPO evidence.

basis: Perinatal gas-exchange failure includes hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy in this record. Direct hypoxic-ischemic renal dysfunction occurs in approximately 40-50%.

decisions.renal: involved: direct renal hypoperfusion and ischemic injury affect approximately 40-50% over the course of clinically significant perinatal asphyxia.

basis: HHV8-associated vascular endothelial sarcoma predominantly arising in skin. Pulmonary and gastrointestinal spread occur in a minority of classic cases.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: the defining vascular endothelial sarcoma arises in cutaneous microvasculature, which falls within the vessel axis.

basis: Tuberculosis is an infection predominantly located in and damaging the lungs; drug resistance does not define additional organ involvement.

decisions.pulmonary: primary: lungs are the predominant anatomical site of tuberculosis, including extensively drug-resistant disease.

basis: Defining cerebral venous arteriovenous malformation; venous hypertension produces hydrocephalus and cerebral dysfunction in roughly 30-50% over the disease course.

decisions.neurologic: involved: cerebral venous hypertension causes hydrocephalus and associated brain dysfunction in roughly 30-50%; intracranial location alone is insufficient.

basis: Microcephaly, intellectual disability and language delay occur in 3/3. Short stature alone does not establish skeletal dysplasia or locomotor dysfunction.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: short stature in 3/3 establishes growth restriction, but the subtype evidence does not establish skeletal dysplasia or musculoskeletal damage.

basis: Immunodeficiency with autoimmunity. Microcytic anemia (2/2) may be secondary; bronchiectasis/bullae (1/2) do not establish direct immune lung injury. Crohn disease and asthma are separate diagnoses.

decisions.haematologic: none: microcytic anemia in 2/2 does not establish direct blood-cell injury; iron deficiency or inflammation associated with Crohn disease may explain it.
decisions.pulmonary: none: bronchiectasis/bullae in 1/2 meet the frequency threshold, but direct immune-mediated injury is unestablished; infection-related bronchiectasis and asthma are separate diseases.

basis: Peroxisomal metabolic disorder; neurodevelopmental impairment, visual disease and hearing loss each commonly exceed 30% in milder Zellweger spectrum disease. Hepatic involvement omitted by cap.

decisions.neurologic: involved: neurodevelopmental impairment and neurologic dysfunction commonly exceed 30%; the defining disorder is peroxisomal metabolism.
decisions.otologic: involved: sensorineural hearing impairment commonly exceeds 30% in milder Zellweger spectrum disease, although subtype-specific frequencies are limited.

basis: Lysosomal storage disease with defining skeletal dysplasia and joint restriction; progressive corneal disease and valvular disease each affect >30%. Common airway disease omitted by cap.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: skeletal dysplasia and progressive joint restriction define the skeletal storage phenotype of MPS VI, including slowly progressing disease.
